title: Slope-Intercept Form
summary: Every straight line can be written as y = mx + b. Two numbers control the whole line.
explanation: m is the slope: how much y goes up (or down) every time x goes 1 to the right.
b is the y-intercept: where the line crosses the y-axis (when x = 0).
Bigger m = steeper line. Negative m = line goes down left to right. m = 0 = flat line.

symbols.meaning: Slope — rise over run. How steep the line is.
y-intercept — where the line hits the y-axis.
Any point (x, y) that sits on the line.

watchFor: Slide m and watch the line rotate around the y-intercept.
Slide b and watch the whole line move up and down without changing steepness.

example.problem: Write the equation of the line with slope 3 that crosses the y-axis at -4.
steps: Crosses the y-axis at -4, so b = -4.

practice.problem: What are the slope and y-intercept of y = -2x + 5?
